questions.label: First crack
questions.prompt: You crack open the cookie and lift the slip. What's the first thing you notice?

options.label: How warm the ink feels, almost like it's thinking
That the words are unusually direct
That it begins softly, like a thought you almost had
That it ends with a turn you didn't expect

questions.label: The trick
questions.prompt: A friend swears every fortune in their cookie is a setup. You...

options.label: Laugh and crack yours open slowly
Read it three times until it fits
Compare slips to find the hidden thread
Turn it over — the back is the real message

questions.label: The notebook
questions.prompt: You've been collecting fortunes in a notebook for years. What's it become?

options.label: A mirror — you can see who you were that year
A map — themes keep circling back to the same streets
A treasure box you open only on hard mornings
A game — you read them backward for jokes

questions.label: Empty cookie
questions.prompt: You crack one open and there's no slip inside. You...

options.label: Take it as a sign — silence is the message
Laugh and assume the kitchen is having a moment
Write your own fortune, fold it, and slip it back
Pass the empty shell to whoever's next to you

questions.label: Friend's fortune
questions.prompt: A friend's fortune is gloomy. They've read it like it's already true. You...

options.label: Crack yours open next to theirs as a counterweight
Point out how fortunes read better sideways
Tell them the one your grandmother always quoted
Sit with them and let the slip stay where it is

questions.label: The tradition
questions.prompt: When you eat the cookie itself, the flavor is...

options.label: A ritual that tastes like a small holiday
A memory of every table you've ever sat at
A treat — the slip is the excuse
A joke — you're here for the crumbs and the laughter

questions.label: Bad fortune
questions.prompt: You crack one open: 'You will fail in a way that surprises you.' You...

options.label: Save it — surprises are how you meet yourself
Re-read it as 'fail freely, without costume'
Crack it in half and read the question mark
Toss it — some cookies came in a bad mood

questions.label: Last cookie
questions.prompt: It's the last cookie from the bag. Who gets the slip?

options.label: Whoever asked first — usually you
Whoever's nearest — slips belong in pairs
Whoever needs it later in the week
Whoever's forgotten to ask

archetypes.label: Classic
archetypes.tagline: Warm, plain, and quietly wise — like the slip you save in a coat pocket.
archetypes.blindSpot: Familiarity can read as comfort when a sharper edge would help.

archetypes.label: Zen
archetypes.tagline: Spare, calm, and certain the empty slip is the point.
archetypes.blindSpot: Stillness can become abstention when the room needs a word.

archetypes.label: Rebel's
archetypes.tagline: Loud, sharp, and unafraid to tell the cookie it got it wrong.
archetypes.blindSpot: Defiance can miss the moment where the small slip was also true.

archetypes.label: Scholar's
archetypes.tagline: Careful, archival, and curious about what the words actually mean.
archetypes.blindSpot: Analysis can outrun the part of the slip that only wants to be felt.

archetypes.label: Heart's
archetypes.tagline: Soft, generous, and inclined to read love into every line.
archetypes.blindSpot: Tenderness can paper over the joke that would have made you both laugh.

archetypes.label: Trickster's
archetypes.tagline: Playful, sideways, and delighted by fortunes that fold back on themselves.
archetypes.blindSpot: Cleverness can keep a friend waiting for the real line that never comes.
